title: Natural Domain and Graph of the Square Root of Absolute Value
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Domain and Graphing
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain and describe the graph of the function g(x) = sqrt(|x|).

steps.title: Determine the Natural Domain
steps.explanation: Because the absolute value |x| is non-negative for every real number x, the square root sqrt(|x|) is always a well-defined real number.
steps.why: The absolute value function maps (-inf, inf) into [0, inf), where the principal square root is defined.

steps.title: Express Piecewise and Check Symmetry
steps.explanation: Since g(-x) = g(x), the function is even and its graph is symmetric across the y-axis.
steps.why: Replacing x with -x leaves |x| unchanged, producing mirror symmetry about the y-axis.

steps.title: Describe the Graph Geometry
steps.explanation: In the first quadrant, the graph is the standard square root curve y = sqrt(x) starting at (0, 0); in the second quadrant, it is the reflected curve y = sqrt(-x), meeting at a sharp corner/cusp at the origin (0, 0).
steps.why: Reflecting the right branch y = sqrt(x) across the y-axis generates the left branch y = sqrt(-x).
